body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), exactly one slice \(M_i\) has rank two, and its label is \(a\); the other two slices have rank three. Every nonzero \(\widetilde k\in\ker(M_a)\) has nonzero coordinates, and \(b\) is the unique label whose coordinate has sign opposite to \(\widetilde k_a\). With \(c=\mathcal V\setminus\{a,b\}\), \(N=\operatorname{adj}(M_a)e_c\), and \(W=M_bN\), \[v=\frac{W_c}{W_b},\qquad u=-\frac{N_aW_b}{N_bW_b+N_cW_c},\qquad \operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v).\] Uniformly on \(\mathcal P_+\), \[|W_b|\ge d_W,\qquad |D|\ge d_D,\qquad |\det(M_b)|\ge d_b,\qquad |\det(M_c)|\ge d_c.\] Thus \(C_3(P)\) globally identifies the labeled chain and both direct coefficients, and \(\operatorname{Rec}\) has constant arithmetic cost.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: skewness alone recovers the unknown mechanism globally rather than selecting among algebraic candidates.
body.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, reports nonidentification through order three on the fixed unrestricted graph; Cai et al. (2023) does not recover this unknown six-chain structure from \(C_3\) alone.
body.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can replace its fourth-cumulant one-proxy initializer by a certified cubic branch on the positive-skew chamber.
